title: An early start on Sunday
setting: Saturday night at the family home. Their mother has the bath ready and Yuki is about to get in, until Kenji comes out of the toilet and pushes in ahead of her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: お風呂できたよ。ケンジは？
lines.kana: おふろできたよ。けんじは？

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.kana: じゃあ、ゆき、さきにはいる？
lines.english: Then do you want to go first, Yuki?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne.
lines.ja: うん、先にお風呂入ってくるね。
lines.kana: うん、さきにおふろはいってくるね。
lines.english: Yeah, I'll go have my bath first.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, matte! boku ga saki ni shawaa abite kuru.
lines.ja: あ、待って！僕が先にシャワー浴びてくる。
lines.kana: あ、まって！ぼくがさきにシャワーあびてくる。
lines.english: Oh, wait! I'm going to go and shower first.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.kana: え、けんじがさき？なんで？

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.kana: あしたはやいんだ。ごめん！
lines.english: I've got an early start tomorrow. Sorry!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.kana: あした？にちようびだよ？

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: okaasan, kiite. kenji, shawaa abinagara uta utatteru.
lines.ja: お母さん、聞いて。ケンジ、シャワー浴びながら歌うたってる。
lines.kana: おかあさん、きいて。けんじ、シャワーあびながらうたうたってる。
lines.english: Mum, listen. Kenji's singing in the shower.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kibun ii n da ne. demo, mou sanjuppun da yo.
lines.ja: 気分いいんだね。でも、もう30分だよ。
lines.kana: きぶんいいんだね。でも、もうさんじゅっぷんだよ。
lines.english: Someone's in a good mood. But it's been thirty minutes already.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: ユキ、お風呂入っていいよ。
lines.kana: ゆき、おふろはいっていいよ。
lines.english: Yuki, you can get in the bath now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: osoi yo! sanjuppun mo nani shiteta no?
lines.ja: 遅いよ！30分も何してたの？
lines.kana: おそいよ！さんじゅっぷんもなにしてたの？
lines.english: About time! What were you doing for thirty whole minutes?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shawaa abite, hige sotte, ha migaite.
lines.ja: シャワー浴びて、ひげ剃って、歯磨いて。
lines.kana: シャワーあびて、ひげそって、はみがいて。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hige sotta no? doko ni hige aru no?
lines.ja: ひげ剃ったの？どこにひげあるの？
lines.kana: ひげそったの？どこにひげあるの？

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: あるよ！ここにちょっと。
lines.kana: あるよ！ここにちょっと。
lines.english: I've got one! A bit, right here.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ha mo zutto migaiteta shi. ne, ashita nani ga aru no?
lines.ja: 歯もずっと磨いてたし。ね、明日何があるの？
lines.kana: はもずっとみがいてたし。ね、あしたなにがあるの？
lines.english: And you were brushing your teeth forever. So what's happening tomorrow?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: nani mo nai yo. a, chotto toire itte kuru.
lines.ja: 何もないよ。あ、ちょっとトイレ行ってくる。
lines.kana: なにもないよ。あ、ちょっとトイレいってくる。
lines.english: Nothing. Oh, I'm just going to the toilet.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: are wa deeto ne. yuki, ofuro haitchatte.
lines.ja: あれはデートね。ユキ、お風呂入っちゃって。
lines.kana: あれはデートね。ゆき、おふろはいっちゃって。
lines.english: That's a date, all right. Yuki, go on, get in the bath.

choices.english: Kenji has to be at school early tomorrow, so their mother lets him use the bath first, and Yuki waits half an hour.
Yuki sings in the bath for half an hour, so Kenji can't get in to shave and brush his teeth before his date.
Kenji pushes in ahead of Yuki and spends half an hour getting ready. He won't say what's happening tomorrow, but their mother guesses it's a date.

questions.explanation: In line 4 Yuki is about to have her bath, and in line 5 Kenji cuts in (matte! boku ga saki ni shawaa abite kuru). His reason in line 7 is an early start tomorrow (ashita hayai n da), but in line 8 their mother points out that tomorrow is Sunday. In lines 9-10 he's singing in the shower and has been in there for thirty minutes. In line 13 he says he showered, shaved and brushed his teeth. When Yuki asks what's happening tomorrow (line 16), he says nothing and escapes to the toilet (line 17), and their mother decides it's a date (line 18: are wa deeto ne). A is wrong: there's no school on a Sunday, and nobody let Kenji go first. He pushed in, and he only showered. B is wrong: Kenji is the one singing and taking thirty minutes, and Yuki is the one waiting.

questions.english: Their mother says the bath is ready and asks where Kenji is. Yuki says "toire itteru yo." Where is Kenji at that moment?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは今どこにいますか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはいまどこにいますか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa ima doko ni imasu ka?

choices.english: He's on his way to the toilet and will be there in a minute.
He's in the toilet right now. He went and hasn't come out yet.
He's in the bath, so Yuki can't use it yet.

questions.explanation: Line 2: toire itteru is iku in its -teru form. With iku, -teru means the person has gone and is there now, not 'is on the way'. So Kenji is in the toilet, and he comes out just in time to push in at line 5. A would be plain toire iku (he's about to go), not itteru. C is the English 'bathroom' getting in the way: in most Japanese homes the toilet is a separate room from the ofuro, so 'go to the bathroom' is toire ni iku. The bath is free, which is why their mother offers it to Yuki in line 3. Kenji's own line 17, chotto toire itte kuru, is the other shape: 'I'm just popping to the toilet (and I'll be back)'.

questions.english: You turn up at Kenta's flat soaked. He asks, "ame ni furareta no? daijoubu?" (Did you get caught in the rain? Are you okay?) Tell him you're fine and you'll go and take a shower.
questions.ja: 雨に降られたの？大丈夫？
questions.kana: あめにふられたの？だいじょうぶ？
questions.answer: Say you're fine, then use shawaa with abiru, ideally in the -te kuru shape: un, daijoubu. chotto shawaa abite kuru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daijoubu. chotto shawaa abite kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。ちょっとシャワー浴びてくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm fine. I'll just go and take a shower.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daijoubu. shawaa abite mo ii?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大丈夫。シャワー浴びてもいい？
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I'm okay. Can I take a shower?

questions.explanation: A shower is water poured over you, so the verb is abiru. abite kuru means 'go and shower, then come back', the shape Kenji uses in line 5 (boku ga saki ni shawaa abite kuru). English 'take a shower' points to toru, but nobody says shawaa o toru. ofuro ni hairu is wrong here too: that's getting into a bath, and Kenta would have to fill one first. The second answer uses -te mo ii? to ask permission, which suits a shower in someone else's flat. Casual speech drops o, as both answers do.

questions.english: Your mother calls out, "ofuro dekita yo. dare ga saki?" (The bath's ready. Who's going first?) Say you'll go and have your bath first.
questions.ja: お風呂できたよ。誰が先？
questions.kana: おふろできたよ。だれがさき？
questions.romaji: ofuro dekita yo. dare ga saki?
questions.answer: Use ofuro with hairu, because a bath is something you get into: watashi! saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: watashi! saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 私！先にお風呂入ってくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Me! I'll go and have my bath first.

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, watashi ga saki ni ofuro hairu ne.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、私が先にお風呂入るね。
modelAnswers.english: Okay, I'll get in the bath first, then.

questions.explanation: You go into a bath, so it's ofuro (ni) hairu, and casual speech usually drops ni. This is Yuki's line 4 (saki ni ofuro haitte kuru ne). Kenji answers it in line 5 with the same frame and the other verb: saki ni shawaa abite kuru. A shower is poured over you (abiru) and a bath is gone into (hairu), so ofuro o abiru and ofuro o toru are both wrong. Their mother uses the same verb in line 18: ofuro haitchatte (go on, get in the bath).

questions.english: It's after lunch at the office, and you get up with your toothbrush. Yuki asks, "a, doko iku no?" (Oh, where are you off to?) Tell her you're just going to brush your teeth.
questions.answer: Use ha with migaku, in the -te kuru shape: chotto ha migaite kuru.

modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと歯磨いてくる。
modelAnswers.english: Just going to brush my teeth.

modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと歯を磨いてきます。
modelAnswers.english: I'm just going to brush my teeth.

questions.explanation: Teeth are polished, so the verb is migaku. Kenji uses it in lines 13 and 16 (ha migaite, ha mo zutto migaiteta). English speakers often say ha o arau ('wash'), but that's for hands and faces (te o arau, kao o arau). Teeth get migaku. With -te kuru you're saying you'll be right back. Lots of people in Japan brush their teeth at work after lunch. The second answer is the polite version, for Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenji what he was doing all that time, and he lists three things. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: shawaa abite, hige sotte, ha migaite.

choices.english: Showering, trimming my beard, brushing my teeth.
choices.romaji: shawaa abite, hige kitte, ha migaite.

choices.english: Showering, washing my face, brushing my teeth.
choices.romaji: shawaa abite, kao aratte, ha migaite.

questions.explanation: Line 13: hige sotte. soru means shaving hair off with a razor, and in line 14 Yuki repeats it to tease him (hige sotta no? doko ni hige aru no?). B is what English 'cut' leads to, but hige o kiru means trimming a beard with scissors, not shaving it off. C, kao aratte (washing your face), is a real collocation, but Kenji didn't say it. Yuki's teasing is about his beard, which she says he barely has.

newWords.english: first, before the others (kenji ga saki? = you first?)
early (ashita hayai = I've got an early start tomorrow)
